learningObjective: Apply the α + βS communication cost model to distinguish latency-dominated from bandwidth-dominated regimes for small vs large collectives.

hardwareContext.architecture: Point-to-point link, α = 10 μs, β = 10 GB/s (⇒ 1/β = 0.1 ns/byte)

stem: A collective has an effective point-to-point cost model T(S) = α + β·S with α = 10 μs and effective bandwidth 10 GB/s (β = 100 ps/byte). Consider two payloads: S1 = 1 KB and S2 = 10 MB. Which statement is correct?

options.text: T(1 KB) ≈ 10 ms; T(10 MB) ≈ 10 μs. Larger payloads amortize α so effectively no time is spent on very large messages, and small ones are dominated by α scaled up by S.
T(1 KB) ≈ 100 ns (bandwidth-dominated at any size); T(10 MB) ≈ 1 ms. Since 10 GB/s bandwidth is high, α is negligible at all payload sizes and the cost ratio equals the byte ratio.
T(1 KB) ≈ 10 μs (latency-dominated); T(10 MB) ≈ 1 ms (bandwidth-dominated). Increasing S1 tenfold to 10 KB barely changes T because α ≫ β·S in this regime.
T(1 KB) ≈ 1 μs; T(10 MB) ≈ 100 s. The bandwidth term should be interpreted as S · β with β=10 GB, giving super-linear scaling with S.

explanation: T(S) = α + β·S. Compute: β = 100 ps/byte ⇒ β·(1 KB) = 100 ps × 1024 ≈ 100 ns, so T(1 KB) ≈ 10 μs + 0.1 μs ≈ 10 μs (α dominates). β·(10 MB) = 100 ps × 10⁷ = 10⁶ ns = 1 ms, so T(10 MB) ≈ 10 μs + 1 ms ≈ 1 ms (β·S dominates). In the small-message regime, S can change by 10× and T barely moves — bucketing is designed to exit this regime.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: units and direction of the model are inverted.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: at 1 KB, α (10 μs) is orders of magnitude larger than β·S (100 ns), so latency dominates.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: matches the two regimes and the (in)variance of T with S when α dominates.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: misinterprets β as 10 GB (giving super-linear scaling).

assumptions: α and β are constants over the size range considered.
nonImplications: Does not imply the crossover S* = α/β is a hardware constant across collectives (algorithms change effective α, β).
Does not imply that a real GPU collective always achieves peak β; contention and topology can reduce effective β.

performanceClaim.scope: α + βS model with α=10 μs, β=100 ps/byte
